Structural API surface designed for a planned `--format json` flag. The file's own JSDoc on `InfoSection` (line 100-102) explicitly states: 'Decoupling this from the renderer means a future `--format json` consumes the same data structure.' `InfoVariantRow` is one of four sibling row-type interfaces (`InfoSection`, `InfoVariantRow`, `InfoOverrideRow`, `InfoReferenceRow`) that compose the exported `InfoOutput` shape — all exported symmetrically as the building blocks of the future stable structured output. `InfoVariantRow` IS used internally on line 128 (`variants: InfoVariantRow[]` inside the `InfoOutput` interface) and the export is the registration point for the planned future `--format json` consumers. The file is NOT in `packages/gazetta/package.json`'s `exports` map today, so this isn't a `public-api` skip — it's planned-feature scaffolding for an upcoming CLI flag, not a current public surface. Knip flagged only `InfoVariantRow` of the symmetric quartet; if the maintainer ever decides to drop the export defensively, the right move is to drop `export` on all four row types together (symmetric refactor) or to ship `--format json` so the exports earn their keep — neither is in scope for a 'this bot deletes; doesn't redesign' run. Precedent: matches the `defaultPreprocessors` skip-entry pattern (top-of-module JSDoc enumerating planned future use) and the `HasDownloadableBrand` situation (knip flagging one of a symmetric type group whose proper resolution is a maintainer-decided refactor). Cost of keeping: one named interface export, type-level only, no runtime cost. Cost of dropping: re-adding it (and the sibling row types) when `--format json` ships, plus surprising the next reader who finds an asymmetric public/private split across the four row types.

rules.reasonNote: Knip's static import graph can't trace three consumption paths for npm dependencies that recur in this monorepo's workspaces: (1) transitive consumption via optional-dep chains — e.g., @floating-ui/dom reaches runtime through @tiptap/react's optional peer @tiptap/extension-bubble-menu, and can silently disappear under `--omit=optional` or `NODE_ENV=production` strict installers; (2) cross-workspace resolution via npm workspace hoisting — e.g., @vitejs/plugin-vue declared in packages/gazetta so its `vite build -c ../../apps/admin/vite.config.ts` script works, resolved from the hoisted root node_modules and invisible to per-workspace import scans; (3) non-code consumption via CDN <link> tags plus CSS-class references — e.g., primeicons loaded from unpkg and used across 131 `pi pi-*` class references in Vue components, with the package.json declaration serving as the version-intent record. Mechanically removing a dep the bot flags in these workspaces could break runtime under stricter install modes, break cross-workspace build scripts that rely on hoisting, or erase version-intent for CDN-referenced packages. The correct resolution is always a maintainer design decision (keep the pin as belt-and-suspenders; drop it and rely on transitive/hoisted resolution; move to peerDependencies; restructure to a bundled import; etc.) — never a mechanical bot delete. This rule replaces three individually-authored skip-list entries with matching rationale: primeicons in apps/admin (added 2026-06-13), @vitejs/plugin-vue in packages/gazetta (added 2026-06-13), and @floating-ui/dom in packages/gazetta (added 2026-08-29). Scope is deliberately narrow (two seen workspaces only); dep findings that surface in tools/, bots/, sites/, or examples/ package.json files earn their own individual skip-list entry, and this rule can widen its scope if the pattern recurs there.
